significance: A group of eight inscribed rock-cut cave shrines cut from a single formation in the Nallamala Hills, dated to the 7th–8th century and compared with the rock-cut work at Mahabalipuram; each cave carries a Brahma-Vishnu-Shiva grouping, alongside life-size dvarapalas, carved lions and Harihara figures, with a 200 m waterfall beside the site. Mahasivaratri and Kartika Purnima draw large pilgrim crowds.
story: Local tradition traces the name to a shepherd, Kalabhairava Kondayya, who made a vow to the deity during a drought.
